audit.finding: FORGE_REWARD_V1 sums transition rewards and carries no term for the value of the resulting world. Branches that end in materially different worlds therefore score identically whenever the flow matched.
audit.telescopingArgument: Both potential terms are differences of a state function, so over a complete trajectory they collapse to Phi(end) - Phi(start) and cannot reorder complete trajectories. They separate only truncated horizons, which is exactly the case the taxonomy found and the case the oracle scores.
audit.note: No component was added to break a tie. The two potential terms measure properties of the resulting world that a flow reward structurally cannot see.

INSUFFICIENT_REWARD_RESOLUTION.why: The branches reach materially different worlds and are STILL different at the end of the horizon, yet every accumulated reward component is equal. FORGE_REWARD_V1 is a pure flow reward: it sums what happened along the way and carries no term for the value of the world it left behind, so two paths with the same flow score the same however differently they end.

HORIZON_ALIASING.why: The branches differ on the immediate step and then genuinely converge: they reach a byte-identical world by the end of the horizon. A property of the horizon length, not of the reward.

GENUINE_STRATEGIC_EQUIVALENCE.why: Different action types reach a byte-identical successor state. The actions are the same move by another name.

ACCIDENTAL_REWARD_COLLAPSE.why: The branches have different reward vectors that the weighting maps to the same scalar. The information exists in the vector and is destroyed by scalarization.

tieTaxonomyBefore.note: Only ACCIDENTAL_REWARD_COLLAPSE and INSUFFICIENT_REWARD_RESOLUTION are reward defects. The rest are properties of the world and must survive any reward change.

diversity.method: min(unique world hashes, unique topology hashes, unique reward rankings). A corpus is only as informative as its least-varied dimension.

difficulty.note: Difficulty is measured by what a myopic chooser loses, not by the level label. A level that is not measurably harder than a lower one is a generator defect.

boundary.note: Every shape is probed below its minimum, at it, just above it, and at two larger sizes. A shape that degenerates at an extreme would produce a mislabelled corpus at that extreme, which is how three Stage 2L generator defects reached certification.

router.note: Ground-truth expert usefulness is derived from world structure by ablation, never from an expert scoring its own relevance. No router was trained.

policyAgreement.note: Sampled during generation. No policy is "the true future": each is a named assumption, and a case where all three agree is stronger supervision than one where they do not.

baseline.oracleUnreachableReason: ORACLE_STRUCTURALLY_UNREACHABLE_AT_TICK_ZERO: decisions are recorded at tick 0, where world.history holds one frame against the Oracle three-frame sufficiency floor.

soup.rlBasis: NOT_APPLICABLE: Soup GRPO/PPO consume prompts plus a reward function, not (s,a,r,s-prime) transitions. The RL export is for Sentinel-side analysis and a future reward-adapter bridge.

baseModelCandidates.reason: Soup ships a validated SFT recipe for it; size fits a single-GPU LoRA run
structured-output bias suits an action-selection format

trainingSubsets.sft: TRAIN split, supervision class UNIQUE_OPTIMUM and EXACT_EQUIVALENCE only
trainingSubsets.preference: TRAIN split, utility gap at or above the predeclared minimum
trainingSubsets.grpo: TRAIN split RL episodes, requiring a reward adapter that does not exist yet

phases.gate: holdout optimum-set agreement must exceed the deterministic Nexus baseline on the same cases
no regression on the SFT holdout gate
blocked until a reward adapter is specified and certified

validationGates: VALIDATION split for model selection; HOLDOUT touched once, at the end
OOD holdout never used during tuning
the deterministic Nexus baseline measured on identical cases, not on a remembered number
no gate may be evaluated on TRAIN
rejectionConditions: no improvement over the deterministic baseline on HOLDOUT
improvement on HOLDOUT but degradation on OOD beyond a predeclared margin
any behaviour requiring authority above R0
any dependence on a Soup artifact that cannot be reproduced from its recorded provenance

targets.uniqueOptimumRateIsConditional: Only if semantically justified. If genuine equivalence remains high the target is NOT forced; the certification records that preference and RL data are the appropriate carriers for those regions.

interpretation.measuredRemainingLimitation: ORACLE_AXIS_UNREACHABLE: every decision is recorded at tick 0, where world.history holds a single frame against the Oracle three-frame sufficiency floor, so the Oracle abstains on 100% of cases. The temporal signal is present in world state (8-18 channel frames per world) and cannot be read by the temporal expert. This is a curriculum defect, not an Oracle defect; the fix is a warm-up of a few ticks before the decision is recorded, which changes every world hash and is therefore a new corpus version rather than a patch to this one. | RESIDUAL_UNRESOLVED_TIES: 2675 corpus cases still carry a tie the reward cannot see. They are routed to RL, not forced into SFT. | CONTINUATION_POLICY_DEPENDENCE_IS_SAMPLED: policy-family agreement is measured on a sample, not on every case, so the invariance rate is an estimate with the sample size recorded beside it. | NO_MODEL_TRAINED: Soup was schema-validated and never invoked. Nothing is claimed about what a trained candidate would do. | ARCHIMEDES_IS_STRUCTURAL_ONLY: there is no Archimedes expert to evaluate, so its router class is a property of the corpus rather than a measured expert usefulness. | SINGLE_PLATFORM: the inherited DIGEST_PRODUCED_SINGLE_PLATFORM limitation is unchanged.
